text:
Maria: quick check-in: ran a mixed-gen workload with node-local affinity turned on and saw asymmetric host-staging activity between NUMA domains. wanted to surface notes and ask for design ideas.
Jon: can you quantify asymmetric? cpu vs io?
Maria: on a 2-socket host, socket-0 had ~70% of staging ops while socket-1 was mostly idle. overall evict rate same but async-migrate backlog on socket-0 spiked. p95 latency for short seqs increased ~22%.
Ash: weird. did the allocator respect per-alloc NUMA hint? we recently changed default to ANY to simplify balancing.
Maria: yes we used default ANY. logs show many allocations getting pinned to socket-0 because the runtime allocated first-fit there and subsequent hotness concentrated. snippet:
```
[2026-03-20T09:11:02Z] alloc: id=0x7f8 tenant=svc-x size=512KB hint=ANY numa_node=0
[2026-03-20T09:11:02Z] alloc: id=0x8a2 tenant=svc-y size=1MB hint=ANY numa_node=0
[2026-03-20T09:11:07Z] reclaim: staged page tenant=svc-x numa_node=0 -> host_pool0
```
Jon: so first-fit + ANY -> locality collapse. we need a smarter placement or a per-alloc round-robin. Also staging pool per-numa warm-pool sizes should be separate to avoid overloading one socket's PCIe path.
Ash: agree. another angle: introduce hysteresis on staging: prefer to stage off different NUMA nodes if the target node's pciq depth > threshold. That would spread load.
Maria: i like hysteresis. also saw that compression on-evict interacts badly with PCIe bandwidth: compressed evicts are CPU-heavy and delay async-migrate queue, making the hot socket worse.
Jon: interesting tradeoff: compression reduces network/PCIe bytes but adds CPU and latency. maybe we should make compression adaptive: if pci_queue_depth > X, compress=false, otherwise compress=true.
Ash: or add per-allocation policy flags: `numa_affinity=PREFERRED|BALANCE|STRICT`, `staging_compress=ALWAYS|ADAPTIVE|NEVER`, `staging_target=LOCAL|REMOTE`. API would let higher layers mark kv-cache entries as BALANCE+NEVER so they get distributed and not compressed.
Maria: that would help. current problem is that higher-level model code can't express such hints. we should expose hints in allocator/placement API and map defaults per allocation class (kv cache, activations, model-params).
Jon: also think about telemetry: we need per-numa metrics: staged_bytes/node, pci_bandwidth_util/node, async_migrate_queue_len/node, and cross-node migration rate. that'll help identify skew quickly.
Ash: testing note: perf harness should simulate interleaved short chats pinned to a subset of cores to reproduce collapse. we can tweak the allocator to do round-robin placement and see effect.
SRE-bot: infra: started canary (numa-hysteresis-v1) on 2 hosts in staging.
Maria: short-term mitigation plan: 1) enable round-robin placement for ANY in canaries (me) 2) add pciq-depth based hysteresis (ash) 3) push telemetry panels for per-numa staging (jon + maria).
Jon: long-term RFC: define per-allocation placement and staging policy spec, mapping for common allocation classes, and a fallback strategy when pci/host paths are saturated. i'll draft.
Ash: also include a small state-machine for adaptive compression toggles and a safe default that prefers latency.
Maria: action items noted. i'll post canary logs after 2 hours with measured per-numa queue depths and p95 latency. thanks. :raised_hands:
Jon: thanks — ping when RFC link is up.
Maria: end note: lesson learned 1 : hardware heterogeneity + simple ANY placement can cause opaque hot-paths; need placement + adaptive staging.
